families.summary: EchoGo Core is standalone software that auto-contours the left ventricle on apical views of transthoracic echocardiograms and reports ejection fraction, Simpson's biplane LV volumes and global longitudinal strain; version 2.0 (K213275) added automatic view classification, A3C support, per-view and segmental strain, stroke volume, LV length and indexed volumes. Anonymized studies are transferred to Ultromics where accredited echocardiographers confirm views and approve contours; the software does not allow manual contour editing.

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Predicate TomTec Arena TTA2 (K150122); reference device Bay Labs EchoMD Automated EF Software (K173780). Differences vs predicate: machine-learning algorithms; no manual contour editing (operator accepts or rejects contour).

families.summary: EchoGo Pro v1.0.2 is standalone machine-learning software that auto-contours the LV on A2C, A4C and mid-ventricular SAX views at rest and peak stress from DICOM stress-echo studies, derives geometric/kinematic features and outputs a two-level categorical assessment of higher vs lower possibility of significant CAD (>=70% stenosis on invasive angiography). Cleared under product code POK using Koios DS for Breast as predicate; a UK 20-hospital RCT (PROTEUS, n approximately 2,200-2,300) did not meet its primary endpoint per ESC 2024 presentation.
families.intended_use_quote: to act as a diagnostic aid using machine learning to assist trained interpreting physicians in analyzing ultrasound images and characterize ultrasound image features for given regions of interest (ROIs) to generate a categorical output
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoGo Pro v1.0.2 is a machine learning-based decision support system, indicated as an adjunct to diagnostic stress echocardiography for patients undergoing assessment for coronary artery disease (CAD). When utilized by an interpreting physician, this device provides information that may be useful in rendering an accurate diagnosis. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the EchoGo Pro v1.0.2 analysis. EchoGo Pro v1.0.2 is to be used with stress echo exam protocols that contain A2C, A4C and mid-ventricular short-axis views at rest and at peak stress. EchoGo Pro vl.0.2 is not intended for the assessment of mild or moderate myocardial ischemia, or localization of coronary artery disease, or for the assessment of myocardial perfusion, myocardial viability or valve disease. Limitations: EchoGo Pro v1.0.2 has not been validated on patients who underwent previous coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery.

families.summary: EchoGo Heart Failure is a fully automated convolutional-neural-network classifier that takes a single non-contrast apical 4-chamber DICOM clip from a patient with LVEF >=50% and outputs 'suggestive' / 'not suggestive' of HFpEF or 'no classification'. Version 1.0 (K222463, Breakthrough designation Q212613) was tested on 1,285 US patients (sensitivity 87.8%, specificity 82.0%); version 2.0 (K240013) added a 0-100% EchoGo Score with histogram display and was tested on 1,578 patients (sensitivity 90.3%, specificity 86.1% excluding no-classification outputs).
families.intended_use_quote: Providing adjunctive information on a patient's cardiovascular condition (diagnostic aid for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)).
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoGo Heart Failure 1.0 is an automated machine learning-based decision support system, indicated as a diagnostic aid for patients undergoing routine functional cardiovascular assessment using echocardiography. When utilised by an interpreting clinician, this device provides information that may be useful in detecting heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). EchoGo Heart Failure 1.0 is indicated in adult populations over 25 years of age. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the EchoGo Heart Failure 1.0 analysis. EchoGo Heart Failure 1.0 takes as input an apical 4-chamber view of the heart that has been captured and assessed to have an ejection fraction ≥50%.
embedded_ai_features: Convolutional neural network (3D CNN per Akerman 2023) classifying a single A4C video clip as HFpEF / no HFpEF / no classification
EchoGo Score 0-100% with 50% decision threshold and histogram comparison to reference dataset (2.0)

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance; predicate Etiometry T3 Platform Software (K213230, PPW) under 21 CFR 870.2200 special controls. Device granted Breakthrough status under Q212613.

Version 2.0: identical indications; adds EchoGo Score (0-100%) with histogram comparison to an independent reference dataset; additional input/output APIs; distributed/replicated deployment options; AI model 'trained on more data and with additional pre-processing steps and data augmentations'; summative human factors testing with 15 board-certified clinicians; test cohort enlarged 22.9% to 1,578 patients.

training_data.description: FDA summaries state independent training, validation and test datasets were used and that v2.0 was 'trained on more data and with additional pre-processing steps and data augmentations' but give no sizes. Peer-reviewed pivotal paper (Akerman 2023, v1.0 development) reports training and validation of 2,971 cases and 3,785 controls (6,756 patients; 16.8% validation holdout). v2.0 training size not disclosed.

validation_data.description: K222463: 1,285 patients (639 controls, 646 cases), retrospective case-control from multiple US sites spanning five states (8 independent clinical sites). K240013: 1,578 patients (785 controls, 793 cases), same design, 22.9% larger; one A4C clip per patient. Race/ethnicity and vendor breakdowns not given in the summaries.

Product page: sensitivity 90.3%, specificity 86.1% (K240013); '10,000+' real-world cases; cloud/PACS integration with results in under 20 minutes; CPT 0932T / APC 5743.

open_questions: Training set size for v2.0 (K240013) not disclosed; only that it was 'trained on more data' than v1.0.
FDA summaries do not report age/sex/race, ultrasound vendor, or image-quality subgroup performance for the HFpEF test cohorts (only the SGLT2i subgroup in K222463).
Abstracts for Cassianni 2024 (JASE) and James 2025 (JASE) could not be retrieved via E-utilities or Crossref; key results not captured.
Definition of the HFpEF ground truth in the FDA test set is not spelled out in the summary (peer-reviewed paper: HF diagnosis + EF>=50% + echocardiographic evidence of elevated filling pressure).
Company press release accuracy figure ('90% accuracy in the validation dataset') is not in the FDA summary.

families.summary: EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0 is a fully automated CNN classifier that takes a single non-contrast apical 4-chamber DICOM clip and outputs suggestive / not suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis (or no classification) as a screening alert for patients aged 65+ with heart failure. Cleared under new product code SDJ with EchoGo Heart Failure (K222463) as predicate; tested on 1,164 patients from 12 US and 3 international sites (sensitivity 84.5%, specificity 89.7%, 14.0% no-classification). The FDA summary discloses training-set demographics (approximately 1,262 controls and 1,302 cases by summing the table) and extensive subgroup performance by sex, BMI, race, vendor, LVEF and wall thickness.
families.intended_use_quote: providing adjunctive information on the cardiovascular condition of a patient
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0 is an automated machine learning-based decision support system, indicated as a screening tool for adult patients aged 65 years and over with heart failure undergoing cardiovascular assessment using echocardiography. When utilised by an interpreting physician, this device provides information alerting the physician for referral to confirmatory investigations. EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0 is indicated in adult patients aged 65 years and over with heart failure. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0 analysis.
embedded_ai_features: Convolutional neural network pre-trained on cases and controls classifying a single A4C clip for cardiac amyloidosis
Input/output APIs and DICOM network interfaces for PACS/ultrasound integration

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance; predicate EchoGo Heart Failure (K222463). Differences: cardiac amyloidosis rather than HFpEF output; population 65+ with heart failure rather than adults >25; no EF>=50% input restriction. Software documentation at Enhanced Documentation level.
notable_flags: Breakthrough Device (per company press release, Apr 26, 2023; not stated in FDA summary)
FDA TAP program (per company: first TAP-enrolled device to reach marketing authorization)

training_data.description: FDA summary: 'Algorithm training data was collected from collaborating academic centres'; training table lists 1,262 controls and 1,302 cases (totals derived by summing the age-band and sex rows on p16; the summary does not print a total), 73% male, 79.7-80.6% White, 13.3% Black, 2.3-3.0% Asian, most aged 61-80; median LVEF 63% controls / 55% cases. 'Independent training, tune and test datasets were used.' Peer-reviewed development paper (Slivnick 2025) reports a multisite multiethnic training set of n=2,612 (52% CA); company press release cites 1,349 biopsy-confirmed cases and 1,263 controls.

validation_data.description: 1,164 patients aged 65+ with heart failure (749 controls, 415 cases), retrospective case:control from multiple sites spanning nine US states; validation cohort comprised 12 US and 3 international sites. Test set 58.4-66.0% White, 24.6-26.8% Black; cases 80.8% male vs controls 47.4%; most aged 71-80; vendors Philips, GE, Siemens, ACUSON. Not evaluated in prior heart transplantation.

Number of sites contributing training data and the reference standard used to define cardiac amyloidosis in the FDA test set are not stated in the summary.

Garmany 2026 abstract refers to 'AI-Echo' without naming EchoGo Amyloidosis; attribution based on Ultromics author affiliation.
